extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, program chairs, and researchers studying conference peer review (ICLR / ML community)
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing which review/rebuttal features and author strategies are associated with reviewer score changes (increase, decrease, keep) in conference peer review, using LLM-based categorization and interpretable prediction models on ICLR 2024–2025 data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating score change
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary target variable: change in reviewers' overall rating score between pre- and post-rebuttal reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis focuses on overall rating changes because most reviews (71% of cases) reflect changes only in the overall score and do not update other aspects such as soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-class / two-class prediction framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of score changes into classes—three-class: 'increase', 'decrease', 'keep'; two-class: merge 'decrease' and 'keep' vs 'increase'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-class yields macro F1 of 0.52; two-class yields macro F1 of 0.71. Use of two-class follows prior work (Huang et al. 2023). Choice affects class balance and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial overall rating (before rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's original overall rating prior to the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong predictor of post-rebuttal score change; authors have limited control over this feature. Initial scores are among the most important features in models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean overall rating of other reviewers (before rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average of other reviewers' overall ratings on the same paper before rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-reviewer ratings are a strong predictor of rebuttal outcomes, indicating substantial peer influence on score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical reviewer score assessing the paper's contribution prior to rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a predictive feature; authors cannot change past numeric scores but can address contribution-related critiques in rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical reviewer assessment of methodological soundness before rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soundness is often not updated in rebuttals; it's an important predictor over which authors have limited control during rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer-reported confidence in their assessment prior to rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a predictive feature; can relate to likelihood of score change after rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement (number of notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of how much the reviewer participates in discussion (e.g., number of notes / replies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer engagement can lead to either an increase or decrease in scores; although authors can respond to engagement, the ultimate effect depends on the reviewer's willingness to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-backed clarification (rebuttal strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing clarifications supported by evidence (e.g., experiments, quantitative results, citations) in a rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual analysis highlights that evidence-backed clarifications and precise responses are most strongly associated with positive score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise responses (rebuttal strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal replies that directly, clearly, and specifically address reviewer concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise responses are associated with positive changes; authors should avoid vague or defensive language and clearly counter factual or methodological misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic / vague defense (rebuttal strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses that are broad, non-specific, or evasive when addressing reviewer critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clearly 'evasive stance' or 'generic/vague defense' tends to only help reviewers maintain their original scores (i.e., associated with 'keep' rather than increases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evasive stance (stance subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking a defensive or non-specific tone that avoids engaging with reviewers' substantive points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with maintaining original ratings; flagged as a strategy that rarely leads to score increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bare agreement / disagreement (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal content that simply states agreement or disagreement with reviewer points without substantive elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing bare agreement/disagreement can help increase scores (when paired with substance); however, bare statements without evidence may be less effective than evidence-backed clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method details (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing additional methodological details (e.g., algorithmic description, hyperparameters, experimental setup) in rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including method details is treated as a strategy subcategory and is among features analyzed for association with score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future promise (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promising future work, experiments, or improvements in response to critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a strategy subcategory; its association with score changes is analyzed (often less effective than concrete evidence-backed clarifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad assertion (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using high-level, general claims in rebuttals without concrete supporting detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as a strategy; broad assertions are less likely to drive positive score changes compared to specific evidence-backed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disagree (stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly disagreeing with a reviewer’s point or assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a stance feature; must be accompanied by substantive justification to be persuasive—bare disagreement is less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness/Strength taxonomy (categories & subcategories)
rubrics_metrics.description: A refined taxonomy of common reviewer-identified weaknesses and strengths (adapted from Gao et al. 2019 and iteratively refined by experts), used to classify review statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories were refined with two academic experts who annotated papers; taxonomy was tested for stability and used to design GPT-4o prompts that achieved 84% pairwise human agreement on validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reviewer-cited weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific recurring criticisms reviewers raise (e.g., unclear writing, weak baselines, limited datasets, unclear algorithmic description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-rated papers are often criticized for these issues; authors should address such weaknesses concretely in rebuttals (e.g., clearer exposition, stronger baselines, more data/analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reviewer-cited strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical praises reviewers highlight (e.g., novelty, methodological soundness, efficient model/approach, clear presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-rated papers commonly exhibit these strengths; emphasizing and clearly documenting them in rebuttals can help maintain or boost scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper borderline status (decision proximity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a submission is borderline between acceptance and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttals primarily affect borderline papers; the study estimates ~20% of accepted submissions likely benefited from rebuttal-driven score increases. Thus, rebuttals are most impactful for near-threshold submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors post or send rebuttal content relative to reviewer activity or deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper examines how timing is associated with impact; timing is a factor authors should consider (analysis suggests timing correlates with effectiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-based categorization reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of GPT-4o to label strategies, strengths, and weaknesses at scale, with iterative prompt design and expert validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM judgments are imperfect; prompts were refined and selected based on highest alignment with manual labels. Reported pairwise human agreement on validation was 84%; caveats about LLM limitations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretable modeling choice (multinomial logistic regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an interpretable classifier (multinomial logistic regression) to predict score-change classes and identify important features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chosen for interpretability to highlight coefficients and top features affecting each class (DEC, INC, KEEP). Data splits, normalization, and grid search over class weights were applied for robust evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model evaluation metric: macro F1
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro F1-score is used to assess model performance across classes, reflecting average per-class F1 without weighting by class size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro F1 reported for both 3-class (0.52) and 2-class (0.71) settings; class size imbalance affects per-class F1 values.
